uncited: Block-based DA-DWT is a segmentation strategy for the Directional Adaptive Discrete Wavelet Transform (DA-DWT) that partitions volumetric data into fixed-size blocks to enable directional adaptivity.
It solves the problem of efficiently selecting optimal wavelet directions for local regions by minimizing the L1-norm of high-pass coefficients.

Unlike its sibling [Segmentation-Driven Directionally Adaptive DWT](7556-segmentation-driven-directionally-adaptive-dwt.md), which allows arbitrary region shapes, this method uses rigid, fixed-sized blocks, trading granularity for reduced signaling overhead.
**Inputs:** Volumetric image data; DA-block dimensions ($N_X, N_Y, N_Z$); set of candidate direction vectors.
**Outputs:** Transformed coefficients; selected direction vector index for each DA-block.
*   **DA-block:** A sub-volume of size $N_X \times N_Y \times N_Z$.
*   **Direction Vector:** A 2D vector representing an angle in the slice plane, indexed from a predefined set.
**Coding:** Encode the selected direction vector indexes and the transformed coefficients.
*   **Boundary Conditions:** The method assumes the volume dimensions are divisible by the DA-block size.
Application of DA-DWT for axial decomposition of volumetric images.
It uses 5x3 or Haar kernels for horizontal/vertical and axial directions.
Optimal directions are selected by minimizing the L1-norm of high-pass coefficients.
Horizontal and vertical decompositions typically use 5x3 kernel with 4 levels.
Coefficients are lossless encoded with code-blocks of $32 \times 32 \times 32$.
A key pitfall is that the L1-norm criterion is only an approximation and may not select the best direction in all situations.
This variant uses tree-based segmentation to measure splitting cost versus coding gain in a rate-distortion optimal way, down to a predefined minimum DA-block size.
Large DA-blocks reduce signaling overhead but decrease adaptability granularity, affecting energy compaction.
This is the core selection mechanism where the L1-norm of prediction (high-pass) coefficients is calculated for all candidate direction vectors.
The vector minimizing this sum is selected.
For a block of size $B$ and $N_D$ directions, the selection cost is $O(N_D \cdot B)$.
*   **Performance:** In lossless compression of volumetric medical images, slice-based DA-DWT has close to no effect on compression efficiency compared to standard transforms.
The method was proposed in the context of wavelet-based volumetric medical image compression.
It builds on earlier work in segmentation-driven DA-DWT and aims to balance adaptability with signaling overhead.
